name: cover-subject
text:
Local Cyber Threat Intelligence
and Incident Response Workspace

alt: Full CyberLens logo: blue-indigo lens mark and CyberLens wordmark

text:
Introduce CyberLens in one sentence: a local workspace that connects asset context, security observations, analyst review, and incident records.

Sources: frontend/public/brand/cyberlens-master.svg; docs/brand-guide.md; docs/architecture.md; student names and registration numbers supplied by the presenters.

name: slide-2-subtitle
text: A local workspace for authorized, evidence-led security analysis.

name: overview-01-body
text: Organize domains, IPs, URLs, emails, applications, and software components.

name: overview-02-body
text: Keep source, time, freshness, status, and evidence references with each result.

name: overview-03-body
text: Link reviewed findings to cases, tasks, remediation plans, and saved reports.

Point out the asset-to-investigation view. The screenshot is an authentic project interface capture using synthetic Demo data; it is not evidence of a live external scan.

name: slide-3-subtitle
text: Security evidence is useful only when analysts can connect it to the right asset and decision.

name: problem-body-0
text: Asset, vulnerability, reputation, and infrastructure details often live in separate tools.

name: problem-body-1
text: Analysts spend time reconciling findings and context before they can prioritize work.

name: problem-body-2
text: A missing result can be mistaken for a clean result when provider failures are hidden.

name: problem-body-3
text: Investigation findings need a review trail and a path into incident and remediation work.

name: problem-takeaway
text: The project focuses on a traceable analyst workflow—not automated verdicts.

Introduce the workflow gap CyberLens addresses: fragmented evidence, manual correlation, uncertain coverage, and disconnected follow-up. Emphasize that the product assists analyst review and does not issue a definitive security verdict.

Sources: README.md; docs/demo-and-viva.md; docs/architecture.md.

name: slide-4-subtitle
text: Build a traceable analyst workflow from inventory to documented follow-up.

name: objective-01-body
text: Keep authorized assets and known software components in one workspace.

name: objective-02-body
text: Run selected checks in background jobs and retain source status and freshness.

name: objective-03-body
text: Treat provider matches as candidates until an analyst reviews applicability.

name: objective-04-body
text: Connect investigations to incidents, remediation work, and point-in-time reports.

name: objective-scope-note
text: Operating principle: analyst-led assessment for assets the team owns or is explicitly authorized to assess.

Describe the project objective as workflow integration rather than automated attack detection. Stress the authorization boundary and human review.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/demo-and-viva.md; CyberLens_Minor_Project_Report.docx, Chapter 1.

name: slide-5-subtitle
text: One workspace links authorized assets to collected evidence, analyst review, and response records.

name: solution-scope
text: Authorized and bounded collection with analyst-led decisions; no exploitation or network-wide scanning.

Present the proposed solution as a shared workbench for an end-to-end analyst process. The collection scope is explicit and bounded; vulnerability candidates and provider observations remain subject to human review.

Sources: README.md; docs/architecture.md; docs/threat-model.md; docs/panel-demo.md.

name: slide-6-subtitle
text: The API persists an investigation before background collectors begin.

name: arch-sources-detail
text:
Demo fixtures or
authorized Live checks

name: arch-takeaway
text: PostgreSQL keeps the record; Redis carries the job; the worker writes evidence back to the database.

Walk left to right. The API writes the investigation and outbox event together. A separate dispatcher enqueues a stable RQ job; the worker runs collectors and persists results in PostgreSQL. Demo uses fixtures; Live uses configured sources only when authorized.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/data-model.md; docs/panel-demo.md.

name: slide-7-subtitle
text: A queued job keeps collection separate from the user-facing request.

name: workflow-asset-detail
text: Choose an authorized asset and scenario.

name: workflow-submit-detail
text: Save the investigation and first attempt.

name: workflow-dispatch-detail
text: Publish a stable job to the Redis queue.

name: workflow-collect-detail
text: Worker records each bounded source result.

name: workflow-report-detail
text: Save a PDF or JSON snapshot.

name: workflow-transaction-note
text: Database transaction → durable dispatch → worker collection → analyst review

Explain that investigation attempts have separate histories and that the outbox/reconciler helps recover delivery. A failed collector means unknown coverage, not a clean result. Analyst decisions are distinct from collected evidence.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/demo-and-viva.md; CyberLens_Minor_Project_Report.docx, Chapter 3.

name: slide-8-subtitle
text: Assets, investigations, findings, and response records connect through stored evidence.

name: graph-note
text: Every relationship points to evidence; this is a PostgreSQL projection, not a separate graph database.

Use this conceptual graph to explain how the modules connect. The implementation stores a typed evidence-linked projection in PostgreSQL; it does not deploy a separate graph database. Change Radar distinguishes new, changed, no-longer-observed, and unknown relationships.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/evidence-graph-interaction.md; docs/data-model.md; docs/known-limitations.md.

name: slide-9-subtitle
text: Containerized local services keep the interface, API, storage, and workers separate.

name: stack-role-4
text: Service orchestration and loopback HTTPS gateway

name: stack-boundary
text: Provider API keys remain in backend configuration; they are not placed in the browser bundle.

Describe the core stack and why jobs are split into dispatcher and worker processes. The app runs as a local single-workspace profile; this is not a claim of public-production readiness.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; README.md; CyberLens_Minor_Project_Report.docx, Chapter 4.

name: slide-10-subtitle
text: Live collectors query selected providers through the backend and save attributable evidence.

name: provider-domain-body
text:
DNS + IANA RDAP
Bounded website / TLS observations
No key; website checks need authorization.

name: provider-vuln-body
text:
NVD / CVE · CISA KEV · FIRST EPSS · OSV
NVD key optional; EPSS and OSV are keyless.
OSV sends package + version only.

name: provider-reputation-body
text:
VirusTotal: existing reports · HIBP: explicit email lookup
VT / HIBP email lookups need provider keys.
XposedOrNot is opt-in and requires consent; HIBP password screening is keyless.

name: provider-feeds-body
text:
Spamhaus DROP + CINS Army: local snapshots
OpenPhish: optional and terms-restricted
MITRE ATT&CK: Admin-triggered catalog sync.

name: provider-mode
text: DEMO: synthetic fixtures only; no external requests.  LIVE: keys stay backend-only; provider access, quotas, freshness, and terms affect coverage.

Use the four source groups to explain which systems are actual APIs, direct protocol observations, or downloaded feeds. NVD API credentials are optional; VirusTotal and HIBP email lookup require their keys. HIBP password screening is a separate keyless range check. XposedOrNot and OpenPhish have additional consent/use restrictions. Feeds are refreshed into local snapshots and then matched locally. Demo makes no provider or website requests.

Sources: docs/setup.md; README.md#use-live-collectors; docs/api.md; docs/xposedornot.md; docs/openphish.md; docs/spamhaus-drop.md; docs/cins-army.md.

name: slide-11-subtitle
text: Each observation keeps its provenance and coverage status as it moves through review.

name: evidence-step-body-0
text: A selected collector runs within its scope.

name: evidence-step-body-1
text: Source, time, status, and freshness are stored.

name: evidence-step-body-2
text: Evidence connects to findings and asset relationships.

name: evidence-step-body-3
text: An analyst confirms relevance and applicability.

name: evidence-step-body-4
text: Reports preserve the reviewed state at creation.

name: evidence-unknown-body
text: A failed, stale, or unrun source is unknown coverage—not evidence that the asset is safe. Evidence hashes help detect byte changes but do not prove authenticity.

Explain the evidence envelope and why the UI preserves statuses. CyberLens distinguishes provider observations, findings, applicability decisions, and saved snapshots. A no-match is not automatically a clean bill of health.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/threat-model.md; README.md; docs/data-model.md.

name: slide-12-subtitle
text: Provider output is an observation to interpret—not an automatic verdict.

name: trust-0-2
text: Keep provider credentials on the backend

name: trust-1-0
text: Store source, time, status, and freshness

name: trust-1-2
text: Hashes detect byte changes; they do not prove authenticity

name: trust-2-2
text: Keep the risk score explainable and explicitly uncalibrated

name: trust-boundary
text: No exploitation · no network-wide scanning · no automatic containment or remediation

A no-match is not the same as unknown. Missing or failed sources stay visible as missing coverage. Vulnerability candidates do not affect vulnerability risk until an analyst marks them applicable. Checksums help detect stored-byte changes but do not establish chain of custody.

Sources: docs/threat-model.md; docs/known-limitations.md; docs/demo-and-viva.md.

name: slide-13-subtitle
text: Workspace access is role-based, session-backed, and recorded for later review.

name: identity-line-1-1
text: Analyst: protected investigation and response writes

name: identity-line-2-1
text: User and role changes are audited

name: identity-boundary
text: Passwords and provider credentials are handled by the backend; roles limit who can make protected changes.

Summarize the protections implemented in the local workspace. Role permissions do not replace deployment security; the project is configured as a local single-workspace showcase, not a public multi-tenant service.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/threat-model.md; docs/setup.md; docs/api.md.

name: slide-14-subtitle
text: The risk view explains its inputs and keeps vulnerability context separate from analyst decisions.

name: risk-body-0
text: Collect source observations and coverage status.

name: risk-body-1
text: Create finding candidates with provider details.

name: risk-body-2
text: Analyst checks whether the finding matches the asset.

name: risk-body-3
text: Versioned policy records a score and its contributors.

name: risk-note-body
text: It is an academic prioritization score, not a probability of compromise or a calibrated industry metric. EPSS is shown separately and does not change the score. Missing coverage stays visible; it is never treated as zero risk.

Explain that the score is versioned and traceable to its inputs. CVSS, KEV, EPSS, source coverage, evidence, and analyst applicability are distinct fields; EPSS does not alter the current score. No calibration claim is made.

Sources: README.md, Risk score and source limitations; docs/api.md; docs/architecture.md.

name: slide-15-subtitle
text: Use the isolated offline Demo profile for a repeatable showcase.

name: demo-text-0
text: Synthetic fixtures; no provider or website requests

name: demo-text-1
text: Repeatable scenarios for success, vulnerability, and outage states

name: demo-text-2
text: Separate Demo Compose project and data volumes

name: live-text-0
text: Uses configured sources and explicit target authorization

name: live-text-1
text: Results depend on provider access, quotas, freshness, and network

name: live-text-2
text: Local showcase profile—not a public deployment

name: panel-flow
text: Routine website  →  vulnerable app  →  applicability review  →  incident case  →  saved report

name: panel-flow-disclosure
text: Identify all Demo findings as synthetic examples.

Recommend Demo for the review panel because it does not depend on keys or external availability. The interface visibly labels synthetic data. Live mode is optional and requires an explicitly authorized target and configured provider access.

Sources: docs/panel-demo.md; docs/demo-and-viva.md; docs/known-limitations.md.

name: slide-16-subtitle
text: Show the end-to-end workflow using repeatable synthetic data.

name: walk-body-0
text: Open a routine website record and show its authorization context.

name: walk-body-1
text: Select the scenario and explain the queued background job.

name: walk-body-2
text: Compare source status, freshness, candidate findings, and applicability.

name: walk-body-3
text: Link a reviewed item to an incident and remediation task.

name: walk-body-4
text: Show the saved report as a point-in-time record.

name: walk-disclosure
text: State clearly: Demo findings are synthetic; no external security checks run in this profile.

Follow this short path during the presentation. Use the project Demo profile and identify the data as synthetic at each relevant screen. The sequence demonstrates product workflow; it is not a real scan or provider validation.

Sources: docs/panel-demo.md; docs/demo-and-viva.md; README.md.

name: slide-17-subtitle
text: Docker Compose keeps the showcase services together on the development machine.

Describe the local Compose profile at a high level. The gateway serves the browser entry point, while internal services communicate on the Compose network. This is a local single-workspace demonstration and not a public production deployment.

Sources: README.md; docs/setup.md; docs/architecture.md; docs/panel-demo.md.

name: slide-18-subtitle
text: Durable delivery and explicit failure states help preserve a trustworthy investigation history.

name: reliability-body-0
text: The API saves the investigation and its queue event together in PostgreSQL.

name: reliability-body-1
text: The dispatcher uses a stable job ID, so a publish retry does not create a new logical run.

name: reliability-body-2
text: Transient failures may retry with limits; permanent configuration errors do not loop.

name: reliability-unknown
text: A missing credential, quota limit, failed source, or stale feed is reported as unavailable/unknown—not silently converted to a safe result.

Explain the split between API request and background work. The transactional outbox and reconciler help recover delivery; retries are bounded and restricted to transient failures. Failed collectors leave coverage unknown.

Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/data-model.md; docs/known-limitations.md.

name: slide-19-subtitle
text: Documented local checks support the showcase workflow; they do not establish production readiness.

name: verification-78-label
text: offline workflow + mocked UI/provider tests passed

name: verification-78-detail
text: Isolated backend workflows and mocked presentation cases · 5.2 minutes

name: verification-1-detail
text: Isolated local login and dashboard · 7.6 seconds

name: verification-build
text: Frontend TypeScript checks and production build passed.

name: verification-limit
text: No live-provider test was run. The risk score is not calibrated; deployment is local and single-workspace.

These figures are transcribed from the dated repository verification record. The 78-test run used isolated offline backend workflows and mocked UI/provider cases; the separate smoke test covered local login/dashboard. No live provider validation was performed.

Sources: docs/test-results.md; docs/ui-final-review-20261026.md; CyberLens_Minor_Project_Report.docx, Chapter 4.

name: slide-20-subtitle
text: CyberLens connects authorized assets, evidence, analyst decisions, and response records in one workspace.

name: next-01-body
text: Evaluate the academic score against a labeled, documented outcome dataset.

name: next-02-body
text: Run controlled integration checks with consent, quotas, and reproducible fixtures.

name: next-03-body
text: Plan managed secrets, backups, monitoring, and tenant isolation before shared hosting.

name: closing-line
text: Asset  →  evidence  →  analyst decision  →  response record

Conclude that CyberLens connects authorized assets, evidence, analyst decisions, and response work in one local workspace. Describe the three cards as future scope: validate prioritization, test provider integrations deliberately, and harden deployment before shared hosting. Invite questions.

Sources: docs/known-limitations.md; docs/architecture.md; docs/test-results.md.
